# TwoSum by ordering: Fast2Sum of the operands ordered by magnitude

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `two_sum_ord` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$a + b$, exactly:

$$s + e = a + b.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`add_down_1`](add_down_1.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$.
- $s + e = a + b$ exactly.
- $(s, e)$ is normalized: $s = \mathrm{RN}(s + e)$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `two_sum_ord_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/DirectedSum.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/DirectedSum.v), against `two_sum_ord_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions two_sum_ord_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition two_sum_ord_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let '(s, e) := two_sum_ord emin prec tie_even a b in
  s = RN emin prec (a + b) /\
  (s + e) = (a + b) /\
  normalized_2 emin prec s e.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `two_sum_ord_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** Fast2Sum of the operands ordered by magnitude (Dekker 1971, with its comparison; [BGM17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#bgm17)). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/two_sum_ord.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/two_sum_ord.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`fast_two_sum`](fast_two_sum.md).

```
# TwoSum by ordering: Fast2Sum of the operands ordered by magnitude, the comparison as two selects
# (milestone2.md, "Rounding a sum down and up"). Unlike two_sum, its error term is finite whenever
# its sum is, so the sign of e can be trusted at the top of the range (decisions.md, the log of
# 2026-11-18). Its IEEE-model statement is that of a finite core: finite operands and a finite
# sum give a finite error term and the claims below. What it returns at an overflow, (inf, -inf)
# with the infinity of the opposite sign, and for infinite and NaN operands (the table of the page)
# is not a claim: the vocabulary has no word for a pair that is not canonical.

aa     = abs(a)
ab     = abs(b)
m      = lt(aa, ab)
h      = select(m, b, a)
l      = select(m, a, b)
(s, e) = fast_two_sum(h, l)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
